claims: "Eid Mubarak" is an Arabic phrase used by Muslims to mean "blessed feast" or "blessed festival".
Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan.
"Eid Mubarak" is commonly used for both Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
"Eid Mubarak" is frequently heard during Eid al-Fitr.
An article from The Columbus Dispatch says Eid al-Fitr celebrates the end of the fasting month of Ramadan.
"Eid Mubarak" is a cultural tradition rather than a strict religious obligation.
It is common for non-Muslims to use "Eid Mubarak" to wish their Muslim friends a happy celebration.
